The electromagnetic field tensor, of which this is a component, transforms covariantly under Lorentz transformations, ensuring that the laws of electromagnetism remain consistent across all inertial reference frames.

E_i.name: E_i
E_i.description: The i-th spatial component of the electric field vector, measured in Volts per meter (V/m).

c.name: c
c.description: The speed of light in vacuum, a fundamental physical constant, measured in meters per second (m/s).

sterile-neutrino-yukawa-coupling-term-1e.title: Sterile Neutrino Yukawa Coupling Term
sterile-neutrino-yukawa-coupling-term-1e.description: This term describes the interaction between left-handed lepton doublets, Higgs doublets, and right-handed neutrinos, which is crucial for generating Dirac neutrino masses via the Higgs mechanism.
sterile-neutrino-yukawa-coupling-term-1e.conceptual_definition: In extensions of the Standard Model, such as those incorporating the seesaw mechanism, right-handed (sterile) neutrinos are introduced to explain observed neutrino masses. This specific term represents the Yukawa coupling that links the left-handed lepton doublet, the conjugate Higgs doublet, and the right-handed neutrino field. It is a fundamental interaction that, upon electroweak symmetry breaking, gives rise to a Dirac mass term for neutrinos, analogous to how other fermions acquire mass.
sterile-neutrino-yukawa-coupling-term-1e.interpretation: This term quantifies the strength of the interaction between the fundamental fields involved in neutrino mass generation. The coupling constant $y_{ u}$ dictates how strongly the left-handed lepton doublet (containing the left-handed neutrino and charged lepton), the Higgs field, and the right-handed sterile neutrino interact. When the Higgs field acquires a vacuum expectation value, this interaction term effectively transforms into a mass term for the neutrino, contributing to its observed mass. The negative sign is a convention, and the overall term is a Lorentz and gauge invariant scalar.
sterile-neutrino-yukawa-coupling-term-1e.limits_and_boundary: This term is valid within extensions of the Standard Model that include right-handed neutrinos. It relies on the electroweak symmetry breaking mechanism for mass generation. The smallness of observed neutrino masses implies either extremely small Yukawa couplings ($y_{ u}$) or very large masses for the right-handed neutrinos, as in the Type-I seesaw mechanism.
sterile-neutrino-yukawa-coupling-term-1e.symmetry_origin: This term is invariant under Lorentz transformations and the Standard Model gauge group $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$. It conserves lepton number if $u_R$ is a Dirac fermion, but can be part of a larger Lagrangian that violates lepton number if $u_R$ is a Majorana fermion, which is essential for the seesaw mechanism.

y_{\\nu}.name: y_{\nu}
y_{\\nu}.description: Neutrino Yukawa coupling constant. A dimensionless parameter representing the strength of the interaction between the lepton doublet, Higgs doublet, and right-handed neutrino.

\\bar{L}.name: \bar{L}
\\bar{L}.description: Left-handed lepton doublet conjugate. A Dirac spinor field representing the antiparticle of the left-handed lepton doublet, which contains the left-handed neutrino and its charged lepton partner. Units: \text{mass}^{3/2}.

\\tilde{\\Phi}.name: \tilde{\Phi}
\\tilde{\\Phi}.description: Conjugate Higgs doublet. A scalar field representing the complex conjugate of the Standard Model Higgs doublet. It transforms appropriately under $SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ to form a gauge-invariant term. Units: \text{mass}.

\\nu_R.name: \nu_R
\\nu_R.description: Right-handed sterile neutrino field. A Dirac spinor field representing a right-handed neutrino, which is a singlet under the Standard Model gauge group. Units: \text{mass}^{3/2}.

ultra-relativistic-limit-of-lorentz-fact.title: Ultra-Relativistic Limit of Lorentz Factor
ultra-relativistic-limit-of-lorentz-fact.description: This expression signifies the ultra-relativistic regime where the Lorentz factor approaches infinity, indicating that the object's velocity is extremely close to the speed of light.
ultra-relativistic-limit-of-lorentz-fact.conceptual_definition: The Lorentz factor, $\gamma = 1/\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$, quantifies the relativistic effects on time, length, and mass. When $\gamma \rightarrow \infty$, it implies that the object's velocity $v$ approaches the speed of light $c$. This limit is crucial for understanding the behavior of particles at speeds where classical mechanics completely breaks down and relativistic effects become dominant.
ultra-relativistic-limit-of-lorentz-fact.interpretation: In this ultra-relativistic limit, time dilation becomes infinite, meaning an external observer would perceive the object's internal clock as effectively stopped. Length contraction also becomes infinite, causing the object's length in its direction of motion to shrink to zero. The object's relativistic mass would similarly approach infinity, requiring an infinite amount of energy to accelerate it further. This regime is characteristic of massless particles like photons or highly energetic massive particles in particle accelerators.
ultra-relativistic-limit-of-lorentz-fact.limits_and_boundary: This represents an asymptotic limit where the velocity $v$ of an object approaches the speed of light $c$. It serves as a theoretical boundary condition for relativistic physics, indicating the behavior of physical quantities as the Lorentz factor becomes unbounded.
ultra-relativistic-limit-of-lorentz-fact.symmetry_origin: While $\gamma \rightarrow \infty$ itself is a limit, the Lorentz factor $\gamma$ originates from the fundamental Lorentz symmetry of spacetime, which is a cornerstone of special relativity. This limit is a direct consequence of this symmetry when velocities approach the invariant speed $c$.

\\gamma.name: \gamma
\\gamma.description: Lorentz factor (dimensionless). It quantifies the relativistic effects of time dilation, length contraction, and relativistic mass increase for an object moving at velocity $v$ relative to an observer.
